summary:
**Conversation Overview**

Bethany runs The Luxora Collective, a consulting business that works with med spas to grow revenue through systems implementation. She works with a team member named Aanchal who handles prospect outreach and sending materials. The conversation focused on building a comprehensive case study library and companion sales tool, all formatted as branded Word documents matching Luxora's navy and gold visual identity.

The session progressed through several distinct phases. Bethany first requested new premium-tier case studies for med spas at the $2.5M revenue level, which Claude generated as illustrative composites covering memberships and package architecture, revenue leak recovery, full growth engine installation, and margin improvement. Claude then integrated the original five foundational case studies Bethany had previously provided into one combined eleven-study document, renumbered sequentially with premium tier first and foundational studies second. Two additional case studies were created mid-session: one addressing front desk staffing and turnover problems, and one addressing the risk of a star injector owning the entire patient relationship.

Bethany then asked whether the combined document gave prospects too much, prompting an honest discussion distinguishing between IP exposure and substantiation risk. Claude clarified that naming capabilities rather than instructions does not give away the methodology, but that fabricated dollar figures presented as real client results create legal and credibility exposure. Claude also raised proactively that the six premium-tier studies were illustrative composites, not measured results, and flagged that the original five foundational studies were the only ones Bethany could actually substantiate. Bethany asked for a selection guide to help her and Aanchal match prospect pain points to the right two or three studies, which Claude built as a separate internal document with a ten-row mapping table, a quick index of all eleven studies, and three rules of use. Finally, Bethany requested all eleven studies rebuilt as individual sendable one-pagers, each framed around its specific issue with a hook callout and relevance line. After reviewing the output she asked Claude to remove the CTA paragraph and Revenue Leak Audit sentence below the client name, keeping only the footer line, so all studies fit on a single page.

Bethany's brand rules applied throughout: no em dashes anywhere, formal full words in documents, no page breaks, ranges written as "x to y" not with en dashes, and the tone stays direct without consultant jargon. She did not raise objections to Claude's substantiation warnings but also did not confirm whether she would act on them. File naming followed a consistent convention: Luxora\_CS01\_Memberships.docx through Luxora\_CS11\_Capacity.docx, with the selection guide saved separately as Luxora\_Case\_Study\_Selection\_Guide.docx and the full combined library as Luxora\_Case\_Studies\_Full.docx.

     5	---
     6	
     7	# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis
     8	
     9	## Overview
    10	
    11	A .docx file is a ZIP archive containing XML files.
    12	
    13	## Quick Reference
    14	
    15	| Task | Approach |
    16	|------|----------|
    17	| Read/analyze content | `extract-text`, or unpack for raw XML |
    18	| Create new document | Use `docx-js` - see Creating New Documents below |
    19	| Edit existing document | Unpack → edit XML → repack - see Editing Existing Documents below |
    20	
    21	> **Script paths:** every `scripts/...` command in this document is relative to **this skill's directory** (the directory containing this `SKILL.md`). Run them from here, or prefix with the skill's absolute path.
    22	
    23	### Converting .doc to .docx
    24	
    25	Legacy `.doc` files must be converted before editing:
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx document.doc
    29	```
    30	
    31	### Reading Content
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	# Text extraction as markdown
    35	extract-text document.docx
    36	
    37	# Show tracked changes instead of accepting them
    38	pandoc --track-changes=all document.docx -o output.md
    39	
    40	# Raw XML access
    41	python scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/
    42	```
    43	
    44	### Converting to Images
    45	
    46	```bash
    47	python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
    48	pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
    49	ls page-*.jpg
    50	```
    51	
    52	`pdftoppm` zero-pads the page number to the width of the total page count (so a 12-page PDF produces `page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`, not `page-1.jpg`). Use the `ls` to get the actual filenames before reading them.
    53	
    54	### Accepting Tracked Changes
    55	
    56	To produce a clean document with all tracked changes accepted (requires LibreOffice):
    57	
    58	```bash
    59	python scripts/accept_changes.py input.docx output.docx
    60	```
    61	
    62	---
    63	
    64	## Creating New Documents
    65	
    66	Generate .docx files with JavaScript, then validate. Install: `npm install -g docx`
    67	
    68	### Setup
    69	```javascript
    70	const { Document, Packer, Paragraph, TextRun, Table, TableRow, TableCell, ImageRun,
    71	        Header, Footer, AlignmentType, PageOrientation, LevelFormat, ExternalHyperlink,
    72	        InternalHyperlink, Bookmark, FootnoteReferenceRun, PositionalTab,
    73	        PositionalTabAlignment, PositionalTabRelativeTo, PositionalTabLeader,
    74	        TabStopType, TabStopPosition, Column, SectionType,
    75	        TableOfContents, HeadingLevel, BorderStyle, WidthType, ShadingType,
    76	        VerticalAlign, PageNumber, PageBreak } = require('docx');
    77	
    78	const doc = new Document({ sections: [{ children: [/* content */] }] });
    79	Packer.toBuffer(doc).then(buffer => fs.writeFileSync("doc.docx", buffer));
    80	```
    81	
    82	### Validation
    83	After creating the file, validate it. If validation fails, unpack, fix the XML, and repack.
    84	```bash
    85	python scripts/office/validate.py doc.docx
    86	```
    87	
    88	### Page Size
    89	
    90	```javascript
    91	// CRITICAL: docx-js defaults to A4, not US Letter
    92	// Always set page size explicitly for consistent results
    93	sections: [{
    94	  properties: {
    95	    page: {
    96	      size: {
    97	        width: 12240,   // 8.5 inches in DXA
    98	        height: 15840   // 11 inches in DXA
    99	      },
   100	      margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } // 1 inch margins
   101	    }
   102	  },
   103	  children: [/* content */]
   104	}]
   105	```
   106	
   107	**Common page sizes (DXA units, 1440 DXA = 1 inch):**
   108	
   109	| Paper | Width | Height | Content Width (1" margins) |
   110	|-------|-------|--------|---------------------------|
   111	| US Letter | 12,240 | 15,840 | 9,360 |
   112	| A4 (default) | 11,906 | 16,838 | 9,026 |
   113	
   114	**Landscape orientation:** docx-js swaps width/height internally, so pass portrait dimensions and let it handle the swap:
   115	```javascript
   116	size: {
   117	  width: 12240,   // Pass SHORT edge as width
   118	  height: 15840,  // Pass LONG edge as height
   119	  orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE  // docx-js swaps them in the XML
   120	},
   121	// Content width = 15840 - left margin - right margin (uses the long edge)
   122	```

   124	### Styles (Override Built-in Headings)

   126	Use Arial as the default font (universally supported). Keep titles black for readability.

   132	    paragraphStyles: [

   134	      { id: "Heading1", name: "Heading 1", basedOn: "Normal", next: "Normal", quickFormat: true,

   141	  },
   142	  sections: [{
   143	    children: [
   144	      new Paragraph({ heading: HeadingLevel.HEADING_1, children: [new TextRun("Title")] }),
   145	    ]
   146	  }]
   147	});

Now for the CTA at the bottom—I need to decide on tone. Since this is a formal client-facing document, I should stick with full words rather than contractions, even though the tagline itself has a conversational feel. Spoken quotes in the case studies used contractions, but these one-pagers won't have dialogue, so I'll maintain formal language throughout. Each CTA will funnel toward the Revenue Leak Audit as the entry point, varying the lead-in but keeping the call consistent. Now I'm setting up the generator and adding a footer with the website.

I'm building a renderOnePager function that generates each case study as its own file, with different layouts for metrics (three columns) versus leak studies (two columns plus totals). I'll organize the data carefully and use the same helper functions, then write out the generator with consistent file naming across all eleven studies.

const styles = { default:{document:{run:{font:"Arial",size:22}}} };

function buildOne(s){
  const children = [];
  header().forEach(p=>children.push(p));
  caseTitle(s.num,s.title).forEach(p=>children.push(p));
  children.push(hook(s.hook));
  children.push(practiceType(s.type));
  children.push(sectionLabel("Challenge"));
  if(s.challIntro) children.push(body(s.challIntro));
  s.chall.forEach(b=>children.push(bullet(b)));
  if(s.impl && s.impl.length){
    children.push(sectionLabel("What We Implemented"));
    s.impl.forEach(b=>children.push(bullet(b)));
  }
  children.push(sectionLabel(s.resultsLabel));
  children.push(s.kind==="leak"?leakTable(s.rows):metricsTable(s.rows));
  if(s.total) children.push(totalLine(s.total[0],s.total[1]));
  children.push(sectionLabel(s.finLabel));
  children.push(body(s.fin));
  children.push(clientLine(s.client));
  ctaBlock(s.cta).forEach(p=>children.push(p));
  const doc = new Document({ numbering, styles, sections:[{ properties:{page:{size:{width:12240,height:15840},margin:{top:1000,right:1080,bottom:1000,left:1080}}}, children }] });
  return doc;
}

(async()=>{
  for(const s of studies){
    const doc = buildOne(s);
    const buf = await Packer.toBuffer(doc);
    const path = `/home/claude/Luxora_CS${s.file}.docx`;
    fs.writeFileSync(path, buf);
    console.log("wrote", path);
  }
})();
